name: Tanning wipes / towelettes

lead: Tanning wipes are pre-moistened cloths impregnated with a self-tanning or bronzing composition, such as DHA, that you wipe over the skin. The payoff is quick, portable bronzed colour without a bottle or mitt.

The chain is the same as other self-tanners: DHA reacts with the dead outer skin layer to give colour without UV, and the colour shows as it develops. A patent filing describes the concept of tissue impregnated with tanning lotion, oil or bronzing agent; no clinical studies of the category were found.

paras: People wipe the cloth over face and body in even strokes, often for travel or touch-ups. Colour develops over hours and fades in about 3 to 10 days.
Uneven wiping can cause streaking or orange colour, and DHA is not approved around eyes, lips or mucous membranes. Bronzers may rub off on clothing.

angle.text: You reach for tanning wipes for a quick, portable way to add bronzed colour without a mitt or bottle. DHA or bronzer tints the skin, and the colour shows as it develops. It is temporary and fades within days.

lead: Tanning wipes, or towelettes, are tissues pre-soaked with a self-tanning or bronzing composition for application by wiping. A patent filing describes a tanning aid made of tissue paper impregnated with a tanning lotion, tanning oil or bronzing agent.
Self-tanning products commonly use DHA, which colours the dead outer layer of skin without UV and fades within roughly 3 to 10 days.[1]
No clinical studies on tanning wipes were found.

paras: A patented concept pairs a tissue with an impregnated tanning lotion, oil or bronzing agent, wiped over the body surface. Wikipedia's sunless tanning article lists creams, lotions, sprays, bronzers and gradual tanners but not wipes.[1]
DHA reacts with amino acids in the dead outer skin layer in a browning reaction, independent of UV and melanin.[1]

Improper application is reported to produce orange or splotchy colour.[1] The FDA has approved DHA for external use but not near the eyes, lips or mucous membranes.[1] Skin may be more UV-susceptible for about 24 hours after DHA application.[1]
